newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian RTS shares index sets new record high.
newsitem.headline: Russian RTS shares index sets new record high.

text.p: The Russian Trading System (RTS) 24-share equities index rose 1.15 percent to 250.55, its third successive record high, on $29.8 million turnover for the entire market, the NAUFOR brokers' association said on Monday.

Most leading shares closed below Friday's levels, partially recovering from a morning fall, and some dealers said the market index gained thanks to demand for secondary shares which have been largely ignored so far in the current rally.
Mosenergo utility had firmed to $1.40 in late trade, up from a morning low of $1.31, but down from $1.42 at Friday's close.
Megionneftegaz oil company rose to $3.95, off a high set during the day of $4.04 but up from Friday's $3.80 close and Purneftegaz oil company rose to $2.84 from $2.75.
"It was a stormy, profitable day. I am bullish," said Deutsche Morgan Grenfell trader Pavel Gronbjerg.

"The blue chips have stabilised, though some may still ease on profit-taking" said Aton dealer Boris Shvedsky. "But second tier activity will be higher," he predicted, estimating that second tiers gained an about four to five percent on Monday.

Shares have seen a bull market since Christmas and volumes have also jumped as experienced funds, followed by new investors, allocated fresh money to Russia, rated 1995's best performing emerging market by the International Finance Corporation.

But Monday's turnover, at the top end of the mid-$20 millions considered healthy for Russia, was still the lowest volume in 1997, which has generally seen about $40 million or more trade. The RTS had a record $58.2 million on Friday.
Many analysts said a correction would be short since there was still hot demand for stocks.
"People tried to bring prices down by holding back demand, but then they realised they cannot buy shares very cheaply," Gronbjerg said.
